title: Uses of chemical reaction
competency: Describe the uses of chemical reactions in everyday situations.

keywords.def: A chemical reaction in which sugars change into alcohol and carbon dioxide.
A process that changes substances into one or more new substances.

en.text: Chemical reactions happen everywhere. Digestion breaks food into small molecules. Burning fuels, smelting iron, making glass and pottery, and brewing are all reactions. Making ammonia gives fertilizer. Photosynthesis keeps the oxygen in the air. Fermentation of tella gives alcohol and carbon dioxide.

screens.title: Making tella
screens.ask: Tella is made by leaving grain, gesho and water for several days. Is that a chemical change?
opts: Yes, sugars change into alcohol and carbon dioxide
screens.after:
Fermentation forms new substances: alcohol and carbon dioxide.
The bubbles and the new taste show it.
It is a chemical change.
screens.best: Yes, sugars change into alcohol and carbon dioxide

screens.title: 3.4.1 Uses of chemical reaction
paras: Chemical reactions happen everywhere, even inside your body.
Digestion breaks large molecules (protein, starch, fats) into smaller ones.
Burning fuels, smelting iron, making glass and pottery, and brewing are reactions.

screens.title: Reactions around you
screens.ask: Tap each one. All of them are chemical reactions.
items: Breaks protein, starch and fats into smaller molecules the body can absorb.
Charcoal, wood and gas burn and give heat for cooking.
Gets iron metal out of its ore.
Heating sand or clay makes new, hard materials.
Fermentation turns sugars into alcohol and carbon dioxide, as in tella.

screens.title: Some important chemical reactions
screens.note: The book prints the sulfuric acid equation with 1 H₂O; the balanced form needs 2H₂O.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A chemical reaction in which sugars change into alcohol and carbon dioxide.

screens.text: Fermentation: what does fermentation in brewing produce?
screens.why:
In brewing, yeast ferments sugars.
Fermentation gives carbon dioxide and ethanol (alcohol).
The carbon dioxide makes the bubbles.
Oxygen and ammonia are not made.
screens.clue: Think of the bubbles in tella.

screens.title: Reaction and its use
screens.why:
Synthesis of ammonia gives ammonium nitrate fertilizer.
Photosynthesis keeps oxygen in the air.
Combustion of methane gives heat from fuel.
Digestion makes food the body can absorb.
screens.text: Match each reaction to its use.
Photosynthesis: true or false? Photosynthesis needs sunlight.
screens.why:
Plants make food by photosynthesis.
Carbon dioxide and water combine in sunlight.
They form glucose and oxygen.
So photosynthesis needs sunlight: True.

screens.ask: Photosynthesis keeps the air steady: our atmosphere is ___% oxygen.
screens.why:
Photosynthesis gives oxygen to the air.
The book says this keeps our atmosphere at 21% oxygen.
So the answer is 21.

screens.text: Review Exercise I 6: respiration changes glucose and oxygen into carbon dioxide and water. Is it a chemical reaction?
screens.why:
Glucose and oxygen are the reactants.
Carbon dioxide and water are the products.
The products are new substances.
So respiration is a chemical reaction: Yes.

test.text: Which of these is a useful chemical reaction?
test.why:
Melting ice and breaking glass make no new substance.
Digestion breaks food into new, smaller molecules.
So digestion is the useful chemical reaction.

test.text: Uses of reactions: ammonia (NH₃) is used to make
test.why:
Ammonia is made from hydrogen and nitrogen: 3H₂ + N₂ → 2NH₃.
It is used to make ammonium nitrate.
Ammonium nitrate is a fertilizer.

6CO₂ + 6H₂O → 6O₂ + C₆H₁₂O₆.
The products are on the right.
O₂ is oxygen. C₆H₁₂O₆ is glucose.
Carbon dioxide is a reactant, not a product.

test.text: Combustion: what does burning methane give?
test.why:
CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O.
The products are on the right.
They are carbon dioxide (CO₂) and water (H₂O).

test.text: Count the atoms: in CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O, how many oxygen atoms are on the right?
test.why:
Count O on the right only.
CO₂ has 2 oxygen atoms.
2H₂O has 2 × 1 = 2 oxygen atoms.
Total: 2 + 2 = 4.
Check the left: 2O₂ = 4. Balanced.

notes.text: The book's sulfuric acid equation 2S + 3O₂ + H₂O → 2H₂SO₄ is not balanced (H 2 ≠ 4, O 7 ≠ 8). Shown balanced with 2H₂O and a note.
